newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold market quiet, awaiting Ramadan boost.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold market quiet, awaiting Ramadan boost.

text.p: In normal year-end fashion, trade in Dubai's gold market was subdued in the week to Sunday with dealers expecting the start in mid-January of the Islamic month of Ramadan to spur activity.
"The market is very, very dull. Everyone is in a festive mood. Everything has been put on hold and we are waiting for 1997 to determine new direction," one said.

"The Dubai market is stagnant. We expect things to get better during Ramadan when retail jewellery sales usually pick up. After good harvests in India, the wedding season there should also buoy demand," another said.

Much of Dubai's demand originates in India, the world's single biggest gold market, and Pakistan. Throughout the Indian subcontinent gold is an important wedding gift and an essential part of any dowry.
"This week has been pretty dead because it is year-end. There is no particular interest from Pakistan or India, but this should pick up during Ramadan," a trader said.
The World Gold Council (WGC) said this week that gold imports into Dubai rose to a record monthly high of 35.50 tonnes in November from 28.41 tonnes in October.
Imports in the first 11 months of the year were 318.52 tonnes, against 318.03 tonnes for the whole of 1995.
"The expectations are that the overseas demand from the (Indian) subcontinent will drive sales in the remainder of the year and early next year," said WGC manager D.V. Pathy.
In line with international gold prices, which kept within a narrow range over the Christmas week, the price of gold in Dubai was little changed.
Traders quoted the benchmark 10 tola bar at 5,105-5,106 dirhams ($1,391) on Sunday, up fractionally from last week's 5,094 dirhams. A ten tola bar is 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold.
On the world market, gold was last traded on Saturday at $369.25/75 an ounce. A week earlier gold traded at $369.00.
